earlier_exploratory_run.note: Before writing the clean scripted run above, this task made an initial exploratory pass with the same OpenAlex query and three separate fetches of the TU/e URL, to characterize the hash-instability behaviour before finalizing the deliverables. Recorded here for completeness, not omitted.

anomaly.description: Five independent fetches of the identical URL (https://pure.tue.nl/ws/files/362308384/3460120.3484819.pdf) by this task produced five different sha256 hashes, none matching the red team's reported hash, despite identical byte count (1,832,736) and identical page-object count (17) in every fetch.
anomaly.diagnosis_method: Byte-diffed tue_paper_a.pdf against tue_paper_verify.pdf (an earlier exploratory-run fetch) with a Python script comparing every byte; 81 differing bytes found, spanning offsets 1,759,432 to 1,832,684 (a ~73KB region near end of file). Inspected the differing region directly: differences are confined to PDF /FontDescriptor /FontName subset-tag strings (e.g. 'JWSTBL+ArialUnicodeMS' vs 'FUXSPD+ArialUnicodeMS').
anomaly.hash_verification_method: sha256 computed three independent ways on the same bytes (sha256sum, openssl dgst -sha256, python3 hashlib.sha256) and all three agreed within each file, ruling out a hashing-tool bug.
anomaly.interpretation_offered_not_asserted_as_f: Consistent with the TU/e repository regenerating or re-embedding font subsets on each request, which would explain a stable byte count and page structure but an unstable sha256. This task does not have access to the server's implementation and does not assert this as a confirmed root cause -- it is the most parsimonious explanation of the observed byte-diff location.
anomaly.consequence: sha256 could not be independently reproduced against RT-20260806-d008e0's reported value with this task's own fetches, and this task's own fetches do not reproduce each other's sha256 either. Route, HTTP status, content type, byte count, page count, and document identity (bookmark/section titles matching the DHKLS paper) all reproduced exactly. Recorded honestly per this task's constraints rather than papered over.

deviations_from_protocol: The handoff's the_correction names 'the returned pdf_url' (singular) from OpenAlex. This task found that OpenAlex's best_oa_location.pdf_url (the most obvious single field) pointed at a paywalled publisher URL (dl.acm.org, HTTP 403) and that the working URL was a different entry in locations[] (index 1, TU/e). This is recorded as a refinement to acquisition_procedure.md, not silently substituted.

This task discovered, and reports as an unexpected observation rather than discarding it, that the TU/e repository's PDF is not byte-stable across repeated fetches of the same URL, so this task's own sha256 does not match the red team's reported sha256 despite matching route, status, content-type, byte count, page count, and document identity.

pypdf (available via pip in this environment) failed to import due to a broken cryptography/_cffi_backend binding; page counting therefore used a raw-bytes /Type/Page object count instead, cross-checked against a /Type/Pages/Count field found in the same files. Recorded as an infrastructure limitation, not worked around by disabling any security check.
